# Pure tensor engineering first observations

`provenance.json` binds two unchanged original preservation archives. They retain
129 frozen sources and diagnostics, plus both original freeze records. The static
reader verifies member names, regular-file modes and hashes entirely in memory;
it neither extracts archives nor executes historical commands, paths or drivers.

The first four open `.qli` functions passed their selected Raw checks. The ordinary
project emission refused the missing closed `main`; that actual diagnostic remains
beside the source. The supplemental desired source was explicitly unexecuted.
Manual original QIRF translations remain separate from source-preservation claims.

The prototype archive retains failed first checker, mathematical and bounded-proof
sources and all actual diagnostics. Repairs never replace those first captures.
The separate supplemental archive preserves rectangular and zero-width owners,
ordered axes, two nonzero budgets, canonical dyadic addition and capacity refusals.
A general final-addition-overflow reachability argument remains unproved; its two
direct arithmetic refusals are not fabricated composed-check failures.

Fresh independent comparisons submit newly authored original small artifacts and
exact requests to the current native executable. The ordered tensor result adds
component budgets without a whole-parent Frobenius check; the I/T tensor identity
at 7/8 distinguishes those routes. Every parent and component is checked afresh,
including original dependencies and full type trees. At epsilon zero the result
still grants no accepted handle, exact cross-artifact equation, inverse/control,
cleanup, target resource certificate or constitutional discharge. Sequential and
controlled composition and source/QIRF/target preservation remain separate work.

`observer-failures.json` separately retains the first integration observer and
actual native/CLI failures. Its first matrix writer mistakenly supplied the
oracle's polynomial coefficients in the wire format's R8 basis; phase-bearing
leaves correctly refused. The next observer used `isometry` instead of the existing
wire spelling `iso`; rectangular inputs correctly failed decoding. The original
observer bytes, both native captures, leaf isolation and first CLI log remain
fixed. Exact basis conversion and the canonical wire spelling repair those
observer errors; neither failure establishes a new semantic rejection rule.
The later 163 fresh native comparisons pass with the separately rebuilt checker.
